title: Mantell UFO incident
operator: 165th Fighter Squadron, Kentucky Air National Guard
summary: Captain Thomas F. Mantell, flying a P-51D Mustang from Godman Army Airfield at Fort Knox, was scrambled to investigate an unidentified aerial object sighted over northern Kentucky. He climbed aggressively in pursuit, exceeding 25,000 feet without supplemental oxygen equipment. Mantell lost consciousness from hypoxia and the aircraft spiraled downward, crashing on a farmstead south of Franklin, Kentucky.
probable_cause: Lack of supplemental oxygen equipment aboard the Mustang, combined with pilot pursuit of an unidentified object to unsafe altitude, resulting in hypoxic incapacitation and loss of control.

notes: Cause clearly established as hypoxic incapacitation

title: BSAA Star Tiger disappearance
summary: BSAA Star Tiger, an Avro Tudor IV aircraft, disappeared without trace over the Atlantic Ocean on 30 January 1948 while en route from Santa Maria in the Azores to Bermuda. The aircraft was in radio contact until approximately 03:15 UTC when radio contact was lost. The investigation found want of care and attention to detail in the flight plan and noted the altitude chosen was much lower than usual. All 31 persons aboard disappeared.

title: 1948 Gatow air disaster
summary: A BEA Vickers Viking airliner on approach to RAF Gatow in West Berlin was struck by a Soviet Yakovlev Yak-3 fighter aircraft. The Soviet fighter was conducting aerobatic maneuvers in the vicinity of Gatow and had not coordinated with air traffic control. As the Viking made a left-hand turn on approach, the Yak-3 dived beneath it and pulled up sharply, clipping the Viking's port wing with its starboard wing. Both aircraft crashed; all occupants of both aircraft were killed. The incident occurred during escalating Cold War tensions over Berlin.
probable_cause: Midair collision caused by Soviet fighter aircraft conducting uncoordinated aerobatics in controlled airspace. The Yak-3 pilot was not under ATC control and failed to avoid the Viking on approach. Soviet aircraft were buzzing American and British passenger aircraft during this period of heightened tensions.

title: Northwood mid-air collision
operator: Scandinavian Airlines System / Royal Air Force
summary: A Douglas DC-6 of Scandinavian Airlines System and an Avro York of the RAF collided in mid-air over Northwood while both holding in a stack at Northolt. The SAS aircraft was ascending through 2,500 feet when the RAF aircraft, despite clearing at 3,000 feet and with possible altimeter error from incorrect QFE setting, descended into the same airspace. title: 1948 Lake Mead Boeing B-29 crash
summary: On July 21, 1948, a Boeing B-29-100-BW Superfortress modified as an F-13 reconnaissance platform for the Upper Atmosphere Research Project completed a high-altitude run to 30,000 feet east of Lake Mead, Nevada. title: Northwest Airlines 421
summary: Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 421, a Martin 2-0-2, crashed near Winona, Minnesota during descent on 29 August 1948. The aircraft's left wing separated in flight due to fatigue cracks in the wing root fittings. A wind gust in the thunderstorm encountered during descent triggered the failure. All 37 aboard were killed. The investigation revealed similar cracks on other Martin 2-0-2 aircraft and recommended increased inspection intervals and lower operating speeds.
probable_cause: The outer portion of the left wing separated due to fatigue cracks in the wing root fittings. The separation was triggered by either a wind gust in excess of design operating velocity, or a similar gust after the material had become fatigued. The investigation revealed fatigue cracks in similar locations on other Martin 2-0-2 aircraft.

title: 1948 Waycross B-29 crash
summary: During a climb to altitude from Robins Air Force Base, a fire and drop in manifold pressure developed in the number 1 engine. Engine number 4 was inadvertently feathered and was not successfully unfeathered prior to the crash. The declassified accident report indicated the fire in engine 1 was likely caused by breaks in the right exhaust collector ring. Non-compliance with Technical Orders 01-20EJ-117 and 01-20EJ-178 existed. The aircraft was not considered safe for flight. Nine of thirteen crew members died and four parachuted to safety.
probable_cause: Fire in engine 1 from breaks in the exhaust collector ring, combined with loss of engine 4 from inadvertent feathering. Non-compliance with technical orders contributed.
